body: A hammer and unopened nails sit beside a note to brace the garden-side door before the next treatment. The note does not say who will return.
title: Fortification order
gloss: A door is reinforced ahead of a treatment, with no return plan.
rival_reading: A response crew might secure a building after any hazard; the timing of the treatment is not recorded.

title: Fortify before the treatment
body: Farm log: “fortify here” meant boards over the garden door before the next treatment truck. The crew promised to collect its sample jars and never returned.
rival_reading: A disaster-response worker could have made the same observation; this personal paper does not identify who directed the work.

title: First heart, clean cot
body: Diary margin: the first heart marks the cot where the orchard crew slept after the spray run. Their boots left a sweet yellow dust; the family returned before anyone posted a warning.
rival_reading: A disaster-response worker could have made the same observation; this personal paper does not identify who directed the work.

title: Second heart, rinsed blanket
body: On the photograph back: second heart, our spare blanket. I rinsed green flecks from it after the seed-treatment men left, then the well began tasting of pennies.

title: Third heart, borrowed room
body: Torn notebook page: the third heart is the room lent to two pasture-test workers. One wrote that the calves refused water before the county cars arrived.

title: Fourth heart, sealed window
body: Personal note: at the fourth heart we shut the window during the field misting. The kitchen herbs curled by supper, hours before the road patrol appeared.

title: Fifth heart, empty cradle
body: Letter draft: the fifth heart was for the baby room. A crop-trial driver warned us not to use the rain barrel, but would not put his warning on the delivery slip.
